findings.reason: The protected SQL solution applies RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(day) ORDER BY amount DESC) inside a CTE to rank transactions by amount per calendar day, filters for amount_rank = 1, and orders the output by transaction_id ASC. Using RANK() guarantees that tied daily maximum amounts are all preserved. The solution is canonical, concise, and optimal; no candidate is required.

Partitioning by DATE(day) correctly isolates full calendar dates regardless of time-of-day. RANK() assigns rank 1 to all transactions matching the maximum amount on that date, so filtering amount_rank = 1 retains all daily maxima including ties.
Partitioned window ranking over r transaction rows takes O(r log r) time, and sorting qualifying IDs takes O(r log r) time. Working space is O(r). Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Outputs single column transaction_id, preserves tied daily maximum amounts, and sorts the output by transaction_id ASC.

The approach accurately details partitioning by DATE(day), using RANK() for co-maxima, and relational complexity bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover MAX aggregation joins, correlated NOT EXISTS queries, ROW_NUMBER tie-loss bugs, DAY(day) month-merging errors, timestamps on one date vs midnight boundaries, tied maxima, single transactions per date, and output sorting.
